newsitem.title: USA: Duke says 93 power restoration after Fran.
newsitem.headline: Duke says 93 power restoration after Fran.

text.p: Duke Power Co, still digging out from under the debris left after Hurricane Fran, said Tuesday it has restored electricity to 93 percent of those customers whose lines were downed by the storm.
"As of 1030 EDT Tuesday, service was returned to about 399,000 customers, leaving approximately 32,000 still to be restored," the company said in a statement.

A Duke spokeswoman, citing company policy, declined to disclose estimated peak power demand on its system now that all its transmission lines are back and service is again available to nearly all of its 1.8 million customers.
"We are expecting temperatures to get up to the mid- to upper 80s (F) this afternoon, with rain across the area," she said.

Over half of the remaining outages are in the Durham, N.C. area, where 20,000 customers were still without service early Tuesday, she said, adding most of these can expect to have power again by the end of the week.
Durham was directly in the path of the storm, which moved north-northwest through the North Carolina after making landfall late Thursday near Cape Fear, N.C.
Duke Power's service territory covers western and central North Carolina and South Carolina.
